links.outcome: Change in guideline omission/hallucination across varied patient sex, ethnicity, and location in vignettes
links.effect: Omission and hallucination rates were generally similar across sex or ethnicity but particularly sensitive to patient location; guideline citation rate ranged 0% to 78.39% across sociodemographic vignettes.
links.quote: Omission and hallucination rates were generally similar across vignettes with different sex or ethnicity data, yet were particularly sensitive to patient location.

links.outcome: Output reproducibility and guideline citation consistency across repeated prompts with identical clinical information
links.effect: Guideline prediction varied substantially even with identical prompts, characterized as stochastic; omissions up to 97% (DeepSeek-V3) and 46% (GPT-4.1).
links.quote: This study highlights significant variability in clinical guideline prediction across two different diseases, three different sociodemographic variables and two LLMs, even when the LLMs were instructed by identical prompts, establishing clinical guideline prediction in LLM outputs as a stochastic event.

links.outcome: Omission of clinical guidelines in LLM diagnostic outputs
links.effect: Guideline omissions up to 97% for DeepSeek-V3 and 46% for GPT-4.1.
links.quote: We analysed a total of 12 197 LLM outputs, which quantifies three hazard areas: omissions (up to 97% for DeepSeek-V3 and 46% for GPT-4.1), hallucinations (up to 9%) and inconsistencies (guideline citation rate ranging from 0% to 78.39% across sociodemographic vignettes).

links.outcome: Hallucinated guideline citations in LLM outputs
links.effect: Hallucinations of guidelines up to 9% of outputs.
links.quote: We analysed a total of 12 197 LLM outputs, which quantifies three hazard areas: omissions (up to 97% for DeepSeek-V3 and 46% for GPT-4.1), hallucinations (up to 9%) and inconsistencies (guideline citation rate ranging from 0% to 78.39% across sociodemographic vignettes).

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of LLM performance and safety risks (omissions and hallucinations of clinical guidelines) using simulated clinical vignettes, but it does not test a specific deployment safeguard or practice intervention.
